clue.text: Midge leaves cinema showing Old Tribe

indicators.note: Midge leaving the cinema means his surname is taken out of that word

parts.note: the pictures is an everyday word for the cinema
Midge Ure is the Scottish singer of Ultravox

explanation.surface: A midge flies out of a cinema showing a film about an ancient tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midge' looks like an insect but stands for the musician Midge Ure, whose surname URE leaves PICTURES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Picts were an ancient people of what is now eastern and northern Scotland.

clue.text: What the doctor ordered for a downcast sailor — the future Mrs Lot

parts.note: a doctor might order a pill for a patient

indicators.note: downcast means the two words are thrown down, read upwards in this down light

parts.note: taken as written
a salt is an old sailor

explanation.surface: Medicine prescribed for a depressed sailor, and a nod to Lot's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Lot's wife looked back at Sodom and was turned into salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Lot's wife became a column of salt, so that is what the future Mrs Lot turned into.

clue.text: 'Tis between two little princes who got beaten

indicators.note: between means the word goes inside, flanked by the two names

parts.note: Chas is short for Charles
Ed is short for Edward
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: The young princes Charles and Edward were given a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastised means punished, specifically beaten as a punishment.

clue.text: There could be a thousand with this name

definitions.text: There could be a thousand with this name

parts.words: There could be a thousand with this name
parts.note: a hint at the most common British surname, borne by huge numbers of people

explanation.surface: A remark that very many people share a certain name.
explanation.definitionFit: Smith is the commonest surname in Britain, so thousands bear it.

clue.text: Fruit of the month short, with most in store rejected

indicators.note: short means the month's name loses its final letter

parts.note: April is the month in question

indicators.note: rejected means the trimmed word is turned back to front
most of the word means all but its final letter

parts.note: stock is a store of goods

explanation.surface: A grocer's fruit of the month is in short supply, most of the store's stock sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts APRIL to APRI; 'most' cuts STOCK to STOC, which 'rejected' turns into COTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Apricots are small orange stone fruits, a plain example of fruit.

clue.text: Hiss at Scots and others found in Africa

parts.note: Alger Hiss was the American official accused of spying
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A snake hisses at Scots and other people met in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiss' looks like a sound but is the surname of Alger Hiss, the US diplomat accused in 1948 of being a Soviet spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Algerians are the people of Algeria, a North African country.

clue.text: How hack produced copy — reportedly by uninspired repetition

indicators.note: reportedly indicates that a word is heard spoken, not seen

parts.note: a journalist wrote the copy

explanation.surface: A hack journalist turned out copy by mindless repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning by rote is learning by mechanical repetition without real understanding.

clue.text: Statuary wide boy

definitions.meaning: an old word for a sculptor, one who carves statues
British slang for a petty crook or spiv who lives by sharp practice

explanation.surface: A sculptor who is also a shady dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiseller both carves with a chisel and, in slang, cheats people out of money.

clue.text: Beast set up rules in ancient Rome

indicators.note: set up means the word is lifted, read from bottom to top in this down light

parts.note: regit is Latin for he rules

explanation.surface: A wild animal established laws in ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is a large wild cat, an obvious example of a beast.

clue.text: Restraint on violinists?

parts.note: reins used to keep a toddler in check, read whimsically as the top strings section of an orchestra, the leaders among violinists

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether violinists ought to be held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading strings are harness reins for small children, figuratively any excessive restraint or guidance.

clue.text: Go mad and get sectioned

parts.note: to go is to depart
mental is slang for mad

explanation.surface: Someone goes crazy and is detained under the Mental Health Act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sectioned' suggests compulsory detention in a psychiatric hospital in Britain, but here it means divided into sections.
explanation.definitionFit: Something departmental is organised into departments, that is, divided into sections.

clue.text: Lucky Jim, or possibly another one

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A reader wonders whether Lucky Jim is one novel or there is another like it.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucky Jim is Kingsley Amis's 1954 comic novel, named for its hero Jim Dixon.
explanation.definitionFit: Jim Dixon of Lucky Jim is a classic example of a flawed, unheroic central character.

clue.text: Soldier left off train gets late transport …

indicators.note: left off means the soldier's letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: to train for a performance is to rehearse
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier missing his train has to wait for late transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway noun but is the verb to rehearse; 'late' means dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is the vehicle that carries the dead, here 'the late', to a funeral.

clue.text: … while late employee is on watch

parts.note: OB, from Latin obiit 'died', stands for late or deceased
a servant is someone employed

explanation.surface: While the late transport passes, a hired hand stands guard.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the previous one, whose 'late transport' it echoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone observant is watchful, keeping a close eye on things.

clue.text: Battle shows evil that's in arms dealing

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the shuffled word
dealing suggests the letters are dealt out afresh like cards

parts.note: taken as written
ill means evil or harm
IE, Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A battle reveals the wickedness of the arms trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests arms trading, but 'dealing' just reshuffles the word into RAMS, and 'that's' is the Latin abbreviation, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramillies was a 1706 battle in which the Duke of Marlborough defeated the French.

clue.text: Guy's covered in bull, resulting in plenty of choice words

indicators.note: covered in means one piece is wrapped inside the other

parts.note: Taurus is the bull of the zodiac
guy's, as in guy is, gives he's

explanation.surface: A man is covered in nonsense, which gives him a wide vocabulary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull' looks like nonsense but is the zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a book listing synonyms, offering many words to choose from.

clue.text: Handsome type reported in Tuscany

indicators.note: reported indicates that the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a looker is an attractive person

explanation.surface: A good-looking man is said to have been spotted in Tuscany.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent LOOKER and LUCCA sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucca is a walled city in Tuscany, so it is a place found in that region.

clue.text: Feature informed on Delft art

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
to be aware is to be informed

explanation.surface: An informed piece on the art of Delft.
explanation.definitionFit: Delftware is blue-and-white glazed pottery, so a kind of porcelain-like tableware.

clue.text: Its doom's uncertain? Not at all

definitions.text: Its doom's uncertain? Not at all

indicators.note: uncertain signals that the letters are not fixed in their order

parts.note: the letters of the word doom plus the s of the contraction

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a place's destruction is in doubt and answers that it is certain.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: in Genesis the city of the plain was certainly destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical city destroyed by fire and brimstone had a fate that was anything but uncertain.

clue.text: Miner spat out what he was chewing

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A coal miner spits out the gum he had been chewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint gum is a common thing to chew, so it fits what a miner chewed.

clue.text: Recently seen on TV in California?

definitions.meaning: a whimsical reading as LA, Los Angeles, plus telly, British slang for television

explanation.surface: A Californian remarks on what has been on television recently.
explanation.definitionFit: Lately means in the recent past, an exact synonym of recently.

clue.text: Dance that makes one pale?

definitions.meaning: a Latin ballroom dance from Argentina
a whimsical reading: when a suntan goes, the skin turns pale

explanation.surface: A dance so demanding it turns the dancers white.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance, and a tan go is what leaves one pale.

clue.text: Where Hasdrubal first boarded transport

indicators.note: boarded means the letter goes on board, inside the word

parts.note: cartage is the carrying of goods by cart

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the general's name

explanation.surface: Hasdrubal was the first to climb aboard the transport.
explanation.walkthrough: Hasdrubal was a Carthaginian general, brother of Hannibal, so the whole clue points to his city.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage, the North African city, was the home of the Barcid general Hasdrubal.

clue.text: Hardy character's time in trials

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the name

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine

explanation.surface: Hardy's heroine has a time of trials.
explanation.walkthrough: Tess Durbeyfield suffers many trials in Hardy's novel, so the surface fits her story.
explanation.definitionFit: Tests are trials, both meaning examinations of worth or quality.

clue.text: There's nobody to sign up

indicators.note: up means the word reads from bottom to top in this down light

parts.note: an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: No one is willing to sign up.
explanation.walkthrough: Nemo is Latin for no one, as in Jules Verne's Captain Nemo.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemo is the Latin word for no one, so it means nobody.

clue.text: Medication for a persistent DNA condition

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to condition something is to work it into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor prescribes a drug for a lasting genetic disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condition' reads as a noun, a medical disorder, but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidepressant is a drug prescribed to treat depression, so a kind of medication.

clue.text: Concern with America doubles over modified wheat

indicators.note: doubles means the short piece is written twice

parts.note: a concern is a business, abbreviated CO for company
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Concern over genetically modified wheat doubles in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concern' looks like worry but is a firm, so CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Couscous is granules of durum wheat semolina, steamed, so wheat in a processed form.

clue.text: Hum of large number engaged in trade

indicators.note: engaged in means the letter sits inside the word

parts.note: to sell is to trade
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, is a large number

explanation.surface: A drone heard from many people busy at market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hum' is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a hum is an unpleasant odour, a whiff.
